initialContact.message: I just got back from my Asia trip and now I have to decide: Start university or keep working? If I start university, I'll make maybe 900€/month (KELA + part-time work) vs 1,800€ now working full-time. That's half the income! But everyone says I need education for good career. Financially, should I keep working and saving, or 'invest in myself' with education? I'm so confused.

problemContext.currentSituation: Gap year student deciding between continuing work vs starting university, weighing income loss
problemContext.emotionalState: torn, uncertain about future, pressure to decide

idealAdvice: This is genuinely tough decision - both paths have merit
Financial comparison:
Option A: Keep working
- Income: 1,800€/month = 21,600€/year
- Living at home: Can save ~1,000€/month = 12k€/year
- In 3 years: Could have 36k€ saved
- Career: Retail management, decent but limited upside
Option B: University
- Income: 900€/month = 10,800€/year
- Student loans: Likely 12-16k€ over 3 years
- In 3 years: Have degree but 16k€ debt
- Career: Higher earning potential (2,500-4,000€ depending on field)
Break-even analysis:
If university degree adds 700€/month to career earnings:
- 700€ × 12 months × 40 years = 336,000€ lifetime difference
- Cost: 3 years lower income + 16k€ debt = ~50k€ total cost
- Return on investment: Massive (336k€ gain vs 50k€ cost)
BUT: This assumes you pick right field and complete degree
Critical questions:
- Do you know what you want to study? (If no: Gap year 2 might be better)
- What career appeals to you? (Determines if degree necessary)
- Are you ready for student lifestyle after earning good money?
- Could you work part-time through university? (Many do)
Alternative path:
Work one more year (save another 12k€), then start university with buffer
This gives you: Clarity on goals + financial cushion + maturity
Age 19-20: Having another gap year is completely fine
Most important: Don't go to university 'because everyone says' without clear goal
But also don't avoid it just because student budget seems tight
The right question: What do you want your life at 30 to look like?
Work backwards from that vision
commonMistakes: Automatically saying 'go to university' without considering her situation
Only looking at short-term income loss, not long-term gain
Not validating that both choices are legitimate
Failing to mention another gap year is option
Missing that uncertainty about major is red flag
Not helping her think about long-term career vision
